key_insight: A reproducible stereolithography workflow can fabricate transparent monolithic porous flow cells that enable direct imaging and pressure measurements, revealing geometry-dependent flow-reversal asymmetry in two-phase flow.
engineering_relevance: This provides an open-source route to rapidly prototype optically accessible porous-media experiments for studying multiphase transport, mixing, and reactive flow in custom pore geometries.
method: Digitally design quasi-2D porous flow cells with prescribed obstacle geometries.
3D print monolithic cells by stereolithography, then flush internal channels to remove uncured resin.
Apply resin coating to improve optical transparency for simultaneous pressure and image-based measurements.
evidence_signal: The proof-of-concept compares triangular and cylindrical obstacle cells using pressure data and image-based active-width measurements for steady oil-air two-phase flow under flow reversal.
watch_item: Transparency and performance depend critically on complete internal flushing and coating, so incomplete resin removal or uneven coating could affect optical quality and flow measurements.
paper_title: Transparent 3D-printed flow cells for porous media studies with proof-of-concept on two-phase flow-reversal asymmetry
